newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK firms plan to invest 6 bln yuan in Shenzhen.
newsitem.headline: HK firms plan to invest 6 bln yuan in Shenzhen.

text.p: Several Hong Kong-based companies plan to invest six billion yuan in real estate in Shenzhen over the next few years, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Friday.

The Hong Kong companies have bought 400,000 sq m (4.3 million sq ft) of land in Shenzhen's Futian district to build residential towers, of which New World Development Co Ltd has 80,000 sq m (860,000 sq ft), the newspaper said.

A group of Hong Kong, foreign and domestic companies plan to invest in a new road linking Shenzhen, just across the Chinese border, and Hong Kong. The project will include a bridge and will cost 2.9 billion yuan, it said but gave no further details.
Hong Kong, which will revert to Chinese rule on July 1 this year, was the biggest investor in Shenzhen last year, it said. The British colony's total investment in Shenzhen is US$7 million, it said.
Earlier this year, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said foreign invesment in Shenzhen rose 39.59 percent year-on-year to a record US$2.422 billion in 1996.
At the end of 1996, the accumulated foreign investment in the city had topped US$11.8 billion, channelled into about 18,000 projects, it said.
